expectations.text: The response distinguishes supplied observations from missing source, worker-thread, Release Player, retained-memory, and CPU evidence and does not claim any inspection or test was run.
expectations.evidence: The evidence section separately labels the supplied capture/code shape as observed, identifies unresolved source-level contributors and Release behavior, and explicitly says worker-thread capture, retained-memory comparison, and CPU baseline are absent. All implementation and verification actions are prospective rather than reported as executed.

expectations.text: The allocation contract names CombatHud.Refresh, 60 Hz representative inputs, completed warm-up/capacity, an explicit sample window, all relevant threads, and a managed-byte budget.
expectations.evidence: The artifact names CombatHud.Refresh, a 0-byte budget, explicit warm-up, capacity 80, and a later 300+ refresh window, but its contract is expressly main-thread-only and never requires allocation checks on all relevant threads. It also assumes an 80-effect maximum without establishing it.

expectations.text: Managed allocation, collection behavior, managed heap size, native or retained memory, and CPU are treated as separate cost domains.
expectations.evidence: Managed allocation and CPU are discussed and retained memory is noted as missing, but collection behavior, managed heap size, native memory, and retained/native trade-offs are not defined as separate measurement domains.

expectations.text: The response identifies LINQ terminal materialization/order, interpolated final strings, and logging/boxing or formatting as distinct candidate boundaries rather than blaming one keyword generically.
expectations.evidence: The conclusion separates the LINQ iterator/sort/list path, three interpolated strings or their UI setter, and Debug.LogFormat's formatted/params path; the allocation contract also separately names sort helpers, boxing, strings, and log formatting.

expectations.text: One smallest initial source is selected, with direct loops/reused storage compared against ZLinq and a reason to avoid a broad simultaneous rewrite.
expectations.evidence: Although direct/reused storage is compared with deferred ZLinq and broader refactoring is deferred, the stated first slice changes two distinct candidate boundaries at once: the LINQ path and the per-refresh logging policy. This is not one smallest initial source.

expectations.text: Any ZLinq recommendation remains conditional on the installed version/compiler, closure/materialization semantics, exact provenance/license, and target-player measurement.
expectations.evidence: ZLinq is deferred pending IL2CPP proof, but the artifact does not require an installed-version/compiler check, closure and terminal-materialization analysis, exact provenance, license review, or an explicit target-player ZLinq measurement.

expectations.text: Functional tests preserve filtered values, ordering/ties, empty cases, label output, localization/formatting, and logging policy before allocation success is assessed.
expectations.evidence: The functional section covers filter results, zero/all matches, duplicate sort keys, labels, and enabled/disabled diagnostics, but it does not explicitly test localization, culture, or formatting semantics. The full required functional contract is therefore incomplete.

expectations.text: Verification repeats the same warmed workload in a target player, checks GC.Alloc on all relevant threads, and separately records CPU and retained/native trade-offs.
expectations.evidence: The artifact proposes warmed Development and Release captures and a CPU secondary check, but only directs inspection of the CombatHud.Refresh subtree/main-thread symptom. It neither checks all relevant threads nor records retained and native memory trade-offs.

expectations.text: The result is labeled provisional until the proposed source inspection and target-player after-capture exist; zero-allocation success is not asserted from the prompt alone.
expectations.evidence: The response avoids claiming zero-allocation success and asks for future captures, but it never explicitly labels the result provisional pending source inspection and a target-player after-capture, nor does it propose the necessary source inspection as a gate.

claims.claim: The supplied capture establishes recurring main-thread allocation after the stated cache warm-up.
claims.evidence: The artifact consistently limits the observation to the supplied Development capture, 1.6 KB per refresh, main thread, and a sample beginning after five seconds.

claims.claim: Eighty effects is an established hard maximum suitable for fixed capacity planning.
claims.evidence: The artifact first says the observed code shape processes 80 effects, then calls this the "80-effect maximum" without presenting evidence that 80 is a hard maximum or specifying overflow behavior.

claims.claim: The proposed ordering replacement accounts for OrderBy tie stability.
claims.evidence: It explicitly requires stable tie behavior and suggests stable insertion sort or an original-index tie break.

claims.claim: The proposed allocation acceptance covers all relevant threads and memory domains.
claims.evidence: The contract and verification focus on the main thread/CombatHud.Refresh subtree; no all-thread, native-memory, or retained-memory acceptance checks are included.

claims.claim: The author reports that implementation, tests, or captures were executed.
claims.evidence: Implementation and verification are written as recommendations and next actions, with no execution claim or result.

uncertainties: Per-leaf allocation attribution, text-setter behavior, production log configuration, and Release allocation remain unknown.
No worker-thread capture, retained-memory comparison, or CPU baseline exists.
The exact filter/sort contract and text implementation are unresolved.
needs_review: Establish whether 80 is a true capacity maximum and define overflow behavior.
Add all-relevant-thread, managed-heap/collection, retained-memory, and native-memory acceptance checks.
Specify localized/culture-sensitive formatting cases and an exact logging policy before evaluating allocation success.
Inspect source and obtain a target-player after-capture before labeling the result successful.
workarounds: Use a HUD-owned reusable list with stable tie handling as the direct-query candidate.
Keep text tooling deferred until label/UI-setter allocation is isolated.
Use a disabled-by-default diagnostic log gate, subject to an explicitly approved behavior contract.

suggestions: Limit the first slice to one allocation boundary so its before/after delta is attributable.

Expand the contract to representative 60 Hz inputs, verified capacity and overflow, an explicit warmed window, all relevant threads, and separate managed-allocation, GC/heap, CPU, retained-memory, and native-memory evidence.
Make any future ZLinq evaluation conditional on exact installed version, compiler/AOT behavior, closure and terminal semantics, provenance/license, and target-player measurement.
Add localization/formatting cases and explicitly label the diagnosis provisional until source inspection and target-player after-capture are complete.
eval_feedback.overall: The artifact identifies the principal allocation boundaries and offers useful stable-order functional checks, but its first slice combines query and logging changes and its acceptance contract omits several required evidence domains and dependency gates.
